findings.why: The new version rewrites a submitted index ('ON wrongtable (title)') into normalized SQL on the collection's own table, so the collection no longer reports the index exactly as submitted; no claim covers this, and it contradicts c2's 'exactly the new set'.

After a rename, the reported index SQL is re-quoted with backticks and now names the new table 'articles' instead of 'posts'; status codes and uniqueness enforcement are unchanged, and no claim describes this rewrite.

A unique index submitted 'ON other (code)' is now stored and returned as '`idx_items_code` ON `items` (`code`)', which changes the reported definition; enforcement is unchanged, and no claim predicts the rewrite.

Index SQL with a schema prefix (main.a1) or double-quoted mixed-case names ("A2") is now rewritten to backtick-quoted, lowercased, schema-less SQL, so it no longer round-trips as submitted; no claim covers this.
Replacing indexes with one on table 'zzz' now stores and reports it as an index on `posts`, which contradicts c2 ('reports exactly the new set of indexes'); no claim predicts the normalization.

On auth collections, index SQL that targets another table (users/members) is rewritten to the collection's own table, and system indexes follow a rename to 'people', so the reported index definitions differ from those submitted; no claim covers this.
